newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Child soldiers disarm in Liberia, process is slow.
newsitem.headline: Child soldiers disarm in Liberia, process is slow.

text.p: A handful of child soldiers handed in weapons in Liberia on Saturday, the second day of disarmament under a peace deal brokered by West African leaders, witnesses said.

But logistical problems and reluctance of fighters to be seen handing in their weapons because they felt ashamed or feared reprisals, appeared to be slowing down the process, U.N. officials and other disarmament monitors said.

Nine child soldiers disarmed to West African peacekeepers in Suehn north of Monrovia on Saturday. "We were ordered by our leader General Alhaji Kromah to disarm to ECOMOG so we came here to disarm," said Malikee Swaray, 14.
Several dozen children handed over weapons in Tubmanburg, Shiefflin camp outside Monrovia and at the Barclay Training Centre in central Monrovia on Friday, witnesses said.
But U.N. officials said only 459 of the estimated 60,000 fighters disarmed on Friday.
The disarmament process, a condition for national election by May 1997, is due to end by January 31.
Freed American slaves set up Liberia in 1847. The war has killed well over 150,000 people. A flare-up in Monrovia in April and May killed hundreds of people, many of them civilians.

Disarmament is part of a peace deal broken by West African heads of state in Nigeria in August, after a dozen previous deals collapsed. They have threatened sanctions against any warlord derailing the deal.
